newsitem.title: USA: World poultry production seen rising in 1997--USDA.
newsitem.headline: World poultry production seen rising in 1997--USDA.

text.p: World poultry production is forecast up 6 percent to 52.5 million tonnes in 1997, supported by a decline in feed prices, the U.S. Agriculture Department said Monday.
China's production would rise 14 percent to 12.5 million tonnes -- 24 percent of world production, USDA said in its monthly World Markets and Trade report on livestock and poultry.
U.S. production would rise 5 percent, the report said.
On the consumption side, China's projected increase in demand for poultry meat is expected to account for nearly half of the gains in global consumption in 1997.
Higher global consumption is supported by large production increases in many countries, implying slightly lower prices, the report said.
The report put U.S. poultry meat exports up 9 percent from 1996 levels.
Chinese exports would be 600,000 tonnes, up from 450,000 estimated for 1996, but China would remain a net importer, with imports at 900,000 tonnes in 1997, the report said.
